packs.title: Rails, Gardens and Hills
packs.promise: Explore San Luis Obispo through separate history, garden and open-space outings.

q.s: Connect one house detail to a documented local industry.
st: Choose one visible exterior detail or a detail in the city's house images.
Identify one Jack family activity documented by the city, such as ranching, banking or land development.
Explain how the detail and the documented activity illuminate different parts of the house's history without claiming they prove each other.

q.s: Compare two documented garden experiences without collecting plants.
st: Choose two open display-garden areas or two areas described by the operator.
Record one visible or documented sensory feature in each, using observation without touching or gathering plants.
Explain how the two features invite different ways of noticing the garden.

q.s: Read a habitat-protecting trail design through the city's account.
st: At the open Prefumo Canyon trailhead or in the city's trail account, locate the hiking-only Bog Thistle route.
Identify one documented habitat the trail passes and one action that protects it.
Make a small route-and-habitat note without touching plants or leaving the designated trail.

packs.title: Mission, Palm and Higuera
packs.promise: Walk connected downtown blocks through public art, history, film and civic places.

q.s: Trace how a civic plaza gives people a safe view of the creek.
st: From an open public path, note one seating or gathering feature and one creek-view feature.
Use the city's plaza information to distinguish a completed improvement from any future plan.
Sketch how the path connects the two features, keeping the Mission museum activity separate.

q.s: Read a public mosaic with its artist and neighborhood context.
st: Find the mosaic from a safe public position or its official art listing.
Credit artist Peter Ladochy and record one material or shape actually visible in the work.
Use the city or downtown art account to explain the neighborhood context, clearly marking any personal interpretation.

q.s: Trace how a temporary street market links growers and visitors.
st: Choose a grower and one other vendor category from a current operator map, or observe them at an open market.
Record where their spaces fall along the Higuera Street blocks without assuming a vendor attends every week.
Draw a two-stop map showing the street's temporary market use and its ordinary public sidewalk use.
